title: The Little Goat and the Highest Mountain

pages.text: This is {name}. {name} is a fluffy white mountain goat kid with two tiny horn-bumps. Out on the green mountain meadow, a little bell goes ding-a-ling!
Every morning {name} looks up at the highest mountain. Its peak hides way up in the sky, behind the very clouds. What could be there, beyond the top?
One morning, while the stars are still fading, {name} tiptoes onto the path. The meadow is fast asleep, and the grass is silvery with dew. Today is a day for a big adventure!
The path winds uphill between grey pebbles. {name} takes tiny steps: clip-clop, clip-clop. And the little bell sings along: ding-a-ling, we're off to see the mountain!
A bright, chattering stream comes rushing down to say hello — cold and merry. {name} hops from stone to stone: splish-splash! Silvery drops tickle their little black hooves.
"Where are you off to so early?" burbles the stream. "To the very top!" answers {name}. The stream is amazed — it only ever runs down.
Beyond the stream lies a meadow, sweet with wild thyme. Sleepy bumblebees are still snoozing inside the flower-bells. {name} steps ever so softly, so nobody wakes up.
By a burrow, a plump marmot gives a big yawn: "My, oh my! The mountain is so big, and the path is long, long, long." {name} smiles back: "That's all right. Step by step, I'll get there."
"Wheet-wheet! Safe travels!" whistles the marmot, and snuggles back down to sleep. Meanwhile the path grows steeper, and the stones grow bigger.
{name} walks on, slow and steady, step by step. Clip-clop go the little hooves on the stones. And with every step, the mountain comes a tiny bit closer.
Up here the wind is fresh, and it smells of snow from the peak. Far below, the meadow looks as small as a green handkerchief. {name} peeks down and whispers: my, how high it is!
On a rock sits a little white cloud, fluffy as a dandelion puff. It is caught on a sharp stone, sighing softly. "I've lost my way to the sky," the cloud whispers.
"The sky is up there, beyond the top!" says {name}. "Come along — we'll go step by step." The cloud gives a happy bounce and holds on softly to the tiny horn-bumps.
Now they travel together: {name} walks in front, and the cloud floats gently above the horn-bumps. The wind gives them a soft push from behind — perhaps it wants to reach the top too.
Little legs grow tired after a while. {name} stops and looks back: my, so many steps already! Each step is tiny — but together they make one long, long road.
A flat, sun-warmed rock is a lovely place to rest. The cloud snuggles close, soft as a downy shawl. One sip of fresh mountain wind — and the strength comes back.
{name} takes a deep, deep breath and calls out: "Hey!" "Hey-hey-hey!" the mountain answers merrily. What do you know — the mountain loves to play echo!
Ahead lies the last climb, the steepest of all. The little bell cheers: ding — one more step! Ding — one more! {name} breathes deeply and keeps on going.
The sky slowly turns pink, as if someone is painting it with a soft brush. The top is almost, almost there. Ten more steps... five... four... wait — three... two... one!
The top! {name} stands on the very tip of the mountain, and the wind gently ruffles that fluffy white coat. And at that very moment, the sun rises over the edge of the world.
Golden light spills out over valleys, rivers and forests. The mountains all around stand like kind sleeping giants. "Thank you! There's my road!" laughs the cloud, and floats up, up into the sky.

And far below, among the golden valleys, {name} spots the dear home meadow. From up here, it is the loveliest place in the whole wide world. So that is what hides beyond the mountain: the great big world, with home right in the middle of it.

Downhill, the path seems to run all by itself, light and merry. The marmot is wide awake now and waves a paw, and the stream laughs: splish-splash, welcome back! {name} rings the little bell in reply: ding-a-ling!

In the evening, the meadow smells of warm grass and home. {name} looks up at the mountain — it doesn't feel far away anymore, it feels like a friend. Because now {name} knows: the highest mountains are climbed with the smallest steps.
